confirmed: Read the entire local markdown, including the references and end matter, and checked the relevant PDF pages directly. The PDF has 15 pages, is published 30 September 2025 and corrected 09 February 2026; the four named authors match the form (PDF p. 1; correction note on p. 14).

No randomized people study is described: everyone performed TCDP first and HAI-CDP second. S1 design_class = quasi_people, assignment.randomized = no, mixed within-process/between-experience structure, and observational context are supported (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 3.2.2 and 3.2.4; p. 8, Table 2; form-spec design_class definition).

S1 includes 42 people, comprising 21 novices and 21 experienced designers; the results also state n = 21 per group. The same people supply both process conditions, so the two arm counts must not be added. Fewer than 50 people were analyzed, no randomized count is supplied, and no exclusions are reported (PDF p. 6, Section 3.2.2; pp. 7-8, Section 3.2.4 and Section 4).

The novices are second-year animation/visual-design undergraduates without real-world project experience; the experienced designers have more than 3 years of relevant work experience. The mixed-population label is supported (PDF pp. 6-7, Section 3.2.2).

S2 consists of interviews with 13 professional designers, each with over 3 years of practical experience, used for qualitative model construction rather than scored creative-output comparisons. The form faithfully retains the malformed duration statement, Each interview lasted between 15 min.; no duration range can be inferred. These interviewees cannot be added to S1 to meet its sample-size criterion (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1).

The character-design task was conducted online; Table 2 specifies 48 h for each process. TCDP used Google Search/Pinterest and Photoshop/Procreate; HAI-CDP used ChatGPT and image generators including Midjourney and Stable Diffusion. The article does not specify their model versions (PDF pp. 6-8, Sections 3.2.1 and 3.2.4; Table 2).

Novelty, quality, and refinement were scored on submitted designs by three blinded experts, using 5-point ratings averaged across raters. Idea count is the number of submitted design outcomes; perceived creative support is self-reported and does not qualify as an output score. Thus criterion_3_outcome_scored_on_output = met is correct (PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 3.2.3-3.2.4).
S1-O1 reported numbers match: novice HAI-CDP novelty M = 3.43, SD = 0.40 versus TCDP M = 1.87, SD = 0.31; process F(1, 80) = 448, p < 0.001 (PDF p. 9, Section 4.2; p. 10, Section 4.3).

S1-O2 reported numbers match: experienced HAI-CDP quality M = 4.36, SD = 0.26 versus TCDP M = 2.49, SD = 0.36; novice paired t = 13.974 and experienced paired t = 21.359, both p < 0.001; process F(1, 80) = 377, p < 0.001 (PDF p. 8, Section 4.1; p. 9, Section 4.2; p. 10, Section 4.3).

S1-O3 reported numbers match: experienced HAI-CDP idea count M = 4.76, SD = 0.89 versus TCDP M = 2.38, SD = 0.50; novice paired t = 8.919 and experienced paired t = 12.619, both p < 0.001; process F(1, 80) = 178, p < 0.001 (PDF p. 8, Section 4.1; p. 9, Section 4.2; p. 10, Section 4.3).

The numerical and substantive content of one_line_finding is correct: 42 designers, a fixed traditional-then-AI sequence, higher novelty/quality/idea count, and reported process F(1, 80) values 448, 377, and 178, all p < 0.001. The ANOVA degrees of freedom are reproduced as printed and do not imply additional independent participants (PDF pp. 6-7, Sections 3.2.2 and 3.2.4; p. 10, Section 4.3).

Core exclusion is supported independently by nonrandom assignment and the sample of fewer than 50 people; observational context remains appropriate. This is an original empirical paper, not a synthesis, and its synthesis defaults are appropriate (PDF p. 1, article type; p. 4, Section 3; pp. 6-8, methods/results; codebook Section 3).

The supplementary material is external and was not read for this check. The main PDF refers to interview materials, statistical analyses, and Supplementary Figures 1 and 2, as the form states; its source.version does not claim these separate materials were read (PDF p. 4, Section 3.1; p. 8, Sections 4-4.2; p. 10, Section 4.3; p. 14, Supplementary material).

No company involvement is disclosed: the funding statement names Hongik University and the authors declare no commercial or financial conflicts. No separate data/code repository URL is provided; the data statement points to the article and supplementary material (PDF p. 14, Funding, Conflict of interest, and Data availability statement).
summary: The fixed-sequence comparison of 42 designers is correctly classified as nonrandomized observational context and excluded from the core dataset. The reported numbers and source version match the PDF, but refinement is omitted, outcome and contrast fields are incomplete, and punctuation is corrupted in several strings.
